lookback_source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

lookback_notes: The section I0100–I8000 (which contains I4900) has two stated look-back periods: diagnosis identification (Step 1) is a 60-day look-back for the physician-documented diagnosis, and diagnosis status active/inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back. The assessor's observation window against which 'active' status is judged is 7 days; the 60-day window applies to identifying that a physician diagnosis exists. The 30-day exception stated in the manual applies only to Item I2300 UTI, not to I4900. The manual does not state how the days are counted relative to the ARD on these pages.

coding_levels.label: I4900 Hemiplegia or Hemiparesis — checked
coding_levels.definition: Check the box for I4900 when hemiplegia or hemiparesis is an active diagnosis (physician-documented in the last 60 days with a direct relationship to the resident's current status during the 7-day look-back period). The section instruction is to check off each active disease and check all that apply.

source.quote: Check off each active disease. Check all that apply.

coding_levels.label: I4900 not checked
coding_levels.definition: Leave unchecked when hemiplegia or hemiparesis is not an active diagnosis; conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the plan of care during the 7-day look-back period are inactive and are not coded.

source.quote: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident’s current status, or do not drive the resident’s plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses.

federal_coding_rules.rule: I4900 is the Neurological-category active diagnosis item for hemiplegia or hemiparesis.

source.quote: I4900, hemiplegia or hemiparesis

federal_coding_rules.rule: I4900 appears in the Active Diagnoses in the last 7 days item set, under the Neurological category, and is coded by checkbox (check all that apply).

source.quote: I4900. Hemiplegia or Hemiparesis

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code the disease only if it has a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days AND has a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Code diseases that have a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days and have a direct relationship to the resident’s current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period

federal_coding_rules.rule: The disease condition requires a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

source.quote: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the plan of care during the 7-day look-back period; these are inactive diagnoses.

source.quote: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident’s current status, or do not drive the resident’s plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Diseases to be coded in a category are not limited to the listed examples; the parenthetical examples are not all-inclusive lists.

source.quote: Examples of diseases are included for some disease categories. Diseases to be coded in these categories are not meant to be limited to only those listed in the examples.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the primary medical condition coded in I0020B is hemiplegia/hemiparesis-related, that primary medical condition must also be included in items I0100–I8000: Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

source.quote: Include the primary medical condition coded in item I0020B in items I0100–I8000: Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: When a Z code is assigned for aftercare following hospitalization, another diagnosis for the related primary medical condition should be checked in items I0100–I7900 or entered in I8000.

source.quote: When Z codes are used, another diagnosis for the related primary medical condition should be checked in items I0100–I7900 or entered in I8000.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If none of the listed active diagnoses (including I4900) apply within the last 7 days, code I7900, None of the above active diagnoses.

source.quote: I7900, none of the above active diagnoses within the past 7 days

federal_coding_rules.rule: Where a practitioner has potentially misdiagnosed a resident with a condition for which there is a lack of appropriate diagnostic information in the medical record, the corresponding Section I diagnosis should not be coded.

source.quote: the corresponding diagnosis in Section I should not be coded, and a referral by the facility and/or the survey team to the State Medical Boards or Boards of Nursing may be necessary.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Stated in the manual's coding tips for Item I5100 Quadriplegia (and therefore relevant when paresis/paralysis results from another condition): for individuals with severe physical disabilities where there is minimal ability for purposeful movement, the primary physician-documented diagnosis should be coded on the MDS and not the resulting paralysis or paresis from that condition.

source.quote: For individuals with these types of severe physical disabilities, where there is minimal ability for purposeful movement, their primary physician-documented diagnosis should be coded on the MDS and not the resulting paralysis or paresis from that condition.

federal.criterion: Physician (or NP/PA/CNS if allowable under state licensure laws) documentation of the diagnosis within the last 60 days; medical record sources include progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, and the diagnosis/problem list (only diagnoses confirmed by the physician may be used from a problem list).

source.quote: Medical record sources for physician diagnoses include progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, diagnosis/ problem list, and other resources as available. If a diagnosis/problem list is used, only diagnoses confirmed by the physician should be entered.

federal.criterion: Diagnoses communicated verbally must be documented in the medical record by the physician.

source.quote: it is also essential that diagnoses communicated verbally be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure follow-up.

federal.criterion: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must be documented in the medical record by the physician.

source.quote: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must also be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure validity and follow-up.

federal.criterion: Evidence of active status must be sought in the last 7 days from: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor's orders, consults and official diagnostic reports.

source.quote: Check the following information sources in the medical record for the last 7 days to identify “active” diagnoses: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor’s orders, consults and official diagnostic reports, and other sources as available.

federal.criterion: Specific documentation by a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist that the condition is active is sufficient and requires no additional confirmation.

source.quote: There may be specific documentation in the medical record by a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist of active diagnosis.

federal.notes: Framed as an indicator that 'may assist assessors' in determining active status.

federal.criterion: In the absence of specific documentation that the disease is active, active status may be confirmed by recent onset or acute exacerbation indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms, and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days.

source.quote: Recent onset or acute exacerbation of the disease or condition indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days.

federal.criterion: Active status may also be confirmed by symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days; a symptom must be specifically attributed to the disease.

source.quote: Symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days.

federal.criterion: Listing the disease/diagnosis on the resident's problem list is not sufficient to determine active or inactive status; the reviewer checks progress notes during the 7-day look-back for treatment of symptoms, doctor's orders for medications, and documentation of physical or other therapy for functional limitations caused by the condition.

source.quote: Listing a disease/diagnosis (e.g., arthritis) on the resident’s medical record problem list is not sufficient for determining active or inactive status.

federal.criterion: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions to manage the condition that requires monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or for potentially severe side effects in the last 7 days supports active status; monitoring of medications for adverse effects alone (pharmacotherapy management) does not.

source.quote: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions to manage a condition that requires monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or to monitor potentially severe side effects in the last 7 days.

federal.notes: Paired with the statement on the same page that nurses' monitoring of all medications for adverse effects relates to pharmacotherapy management, not to management/monitoring of the underlying disease.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages do not tie item I4900 to any payment or case-mix classification. The only payment-related reference in this excerpt is item I0020 (primary medical condition category for the Medicare Part A stay), which is a different item.

conflicts.topic: Two look-back windows apply to the I0100–I8000 active diagnosis items, including I4900

positions.claim: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) uses a 60-day look-back period for the physician-documented diagnosis.

source.quote: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) is a 60-day look-back period.

positions.claim: Diagnosis status (active or inactive, Step 2) uses a 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: the manual states both windows apply in sequence — a diagnosis documented in the last 60 days must also be active during the 7-day look-back period (p. I-9). The assessor's observation window recorded in lookback_days is 7 days.

not_found: item-specific coding instructions or examples for I4900 (the pages provide only the item listing and section-level rules)
